metaDescription: Six large electric griddles at the upper budget cap, from 20 to 22 inch plates to a warming-tray model, built for family breakfasts and weekend crowds.
introParagraphs: The upper budget cap is where electric griddles stop being breakfast gadgets and start being entertaining tools. Plates here reach 20 and 22 inches, one model adds a warming tray, and a few carry detachable handles meant to help the whole thing slide into a cupboard. The question shifts from how big you can afford to how big you can really live with.

Size carries a hidden cost. A 22 inch plate needs generous counter space while it heats and a wide shelf when it does not, and some cool-touch designs and drip trays get dropped as plates grow. Ceramic nonstick coatings are common at this tier, which means nylon or wooden tools, a full cool-down before washing and a little patience with new surfaces.

We evaluated each pick from the product listing and recurring buyer feedback themes, choosing six that make distinct offers: probe-controlled plates, a warming-tray combo, a pull-out drip tray, a buffet-style low profile and a 1500 watt powerhouse. Every one sits at or under the cap, and we say so when a listing is silent on a detail such as a drain.

products.name: bella 12 x 22 Inch Ceramic Electric Griddle
products.description:
The bella 12 by 22 inch is the best-balanced large griddle at this cap. It offers one of the biggest plates in the group, with room for up to 15 eggs or 8 pancakes at once, and the EverGood ceramic coating is described as releasing food readily. A removable probe sets the heat, and the parts are listed as dishwasher-safe.

Big plates need big storage. The body is large enough to want a dedicated shelf, and the probe must be seated before every cook. The listing does not mention a drip tray, so greasy foods rely on your own blotting.

In use, it is the one you pull out for holiday mornings and weekend brunch. It outclasses the 20 inch Presto in area and sits well above the smaller bella 10 by 20 in capacity. The extra 2 inches of width compared with that model make a real difference when you flip pancakes in rows.
products.bestFor: Large families and brunch hosts who want maximum area with easy cleanup.
pros: Handles up to 15 eggs or 8 pancakes
Ceramic coating releases food easily
Removable probe sets heat precisely
Dishwasher-safe parts shorten cleanup
cons: Large body needs a big storage shelf
Probe must be seated before cooking

products.name: bella 12 x 22 Inch Griddle with Warming Tray
products.description:
This bella adds a feature none of the others have: an electric warming tray. The listing describes it as BPA-free and dishwasher-safe, and says it keeps cooked food ready to serve while the next batch cooks. The main plate is the same 12 by 22 inch size, with room for up to 15 eggs or 8 pancakes.

The extra piece means extra footprint. You need somewhere to keep the tray, and the combined setup takes more counter than the plain version. If you rarely cook more than one batch, the tray sits idle.

It shines at the hosting stage, where the first round of pancakes can wait warm instead of going cold on a plate. Compared with the standard bella 12 by 22 inch, you pay in space for convenience at the table. For anyone cooking in waves, that is a fair trade.
products.bestFor: Brunch hosts who cook in batches and need food kept warm.

products.name: Gourmia 22 Inch XL Ceramic Electric Griddle
products.description:
Gourmia pairs a 22 inch plate with a pull-out drip tray, which is the combination that suits bacon and sausage at scale. The ceramic flat top is described as easy to wipe, and the temperature range runs from 200 to 400F, wide enough to span warming to browning.

The listing says nothing about a cool-touch base, so the exterior may get warm, and a surface this large demands real counter space. It also lacks the detachable handles of the Presto models.

In practice the pull-out tray is the feature to appreciate: fat runs off the plate and into a container you can slide out and empty. Next to the bella with its warming tray, the Gourmia puts grease control ahead of keeping food warm. If your family cooks a lot of bacon, this is the cleaner way to do it.
products.bestFor: Big bacon and sausage breakfasts that generate a lot of fat.
pros: Plate is large enough to feed a family
Pull-out tray keeps grease contained
Range of 200 to 400F covers most cooking
Ceramic top wipes clean without effort
cons: No cool-touch base mentioned in the listing
Large size needs real counter space

products.name: Presto 07062 22 Inch Ceramic Electric Griddle
products.description:
Presto 07062 is the large griddle designed with the cupboard in mind. Its handles come off to make storage compact, the 22 inch plate has a textured ceramic surface said to improve release, and the listing pitches it for every meal, not just breakfast.

There is a routine to follow. Handles must be attached before each use, ceramic needs soft utensils and the plate is big enough to need generous counter room. The listing mentions no probe or drip tray detail.

Ownership comes down to the shelf. Removing the handles shrinks the footprint, which is a real help in a small kitchen with a big appetite. Compared with the Gourmia, which gives you a drip tray, the Presto gives you storage flexibility. Pick it when cupboard space is your limiting factor.
products.bestFor: Cooks with a big appetite and a small cupboard.
pros: Extra-large plate suits big batches
Textured ceramic helps food release
Removable handles ease storage and cleaning
Works for lunch and dinner as well as breakfast
cons: Handles must be attached before every use

products.name: Presto 07030 20 Inch Cool Touch Electric Griddle
products.description:
Presto 07030 is built for serving as well as cooking. The 20 inch plate sits in a low-profile cool-touch body that works on a buffet table, and the ceramic surface is described as PFAS-free. It is pitched at breakfast, lunch and dinner.

The listing mentions no drain or grease channel, the body is awkward in a small cupboard and the plate is too large for single-person cooking. Because it lacks a probe in the description, check the control details before relying on it.

Its best use is on a sideboard, where guests can serve themselves from the hot plate. For daily cooking it is bigger than most households need. Choose it for gatherings, and choose a different pick if you value grease control.
products.bestFor: Buffet-style serving at gatherings and potlucks.

products.name: bella XL Ceramic Titanium Electric Griddle
products.description:
The bella XL leads on stated power. A 1500 watt heating system warms an extra-large plate, the listing says it cooks up to 15 eggs at once and cool-touch handles make it easier to move. A ceramic titanium coating handles nonstick duty, and a built-in ledge on the base helps keep food on the plate.

The listing mentions no removable control and no drip tray, so grease and cleaning rely on wiping. A plate this large also takes real shelf and counter room.

For busy mornings it is the model that heats quickest, which matters when you cook in several batches. Compared with the standard bella 12 by 22 inch, you give up the removable probe, though you gain the stated wattage. Pick it if heat recovery matters more than a washable control.
products.bestFor: Fast, repeated batches where heat recovery matters.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Plates at this tier reach 20 and 22 inches. The bella 12 by 22 inch cooks up to 15 eggs or 8 pancakes, while the Presto 07030 at 20 inches suits buffets. Measure your counter and cupboard before choosing. If the plate lives on the counter all year, you have bought the wrong size.

Detachable handles shrink a big griddle for storage. The Presto 07062 removes its handles to fit a standard cupboard, while the bella warming tray model adds a piece to store. Consider where it will live between uses.

Fat on a large plate is a mess unless it drains. The Gourmia 22 inch has a pull-out drip tray, while the Presto models and the bella list none. If you cook bacon often, put drainage near the top of your list.

More area needs more heat. The bella XL lists 1500 watts, and the Gourmia gives a range of 200 to 400F. Even heating matters more than the peak number on a long plate, so favor listings that mention edge-to-edge coverage.

Ceramic surfaces need soft tools and a full cool-down before washing. Presto textures its surface for release, and the bella uses EverGood coating. Avoid abrasive pads and metal scrapers, which shorten the life of any ceramic.

A warming tray, a low profile or cool-touch handles change how the griddle works at the table. The bella warming tray model holds food warm, the Presto 07030 is built for buffets, and the bella XL has cool-touch handles. Decide whether you cook alone or serve a crowd.

howWeEvaluated.title: Plate area and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated sizes and egg or pancake counts. The bella 12 by 22 inch models and the Gourmia 22 inch lead on area, the Presto 07062 offers 22 inches and the Presto 07030 offers 20.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: Dishwasher-safe parts, removable handles and warming trays were weighed against the bulk they add. The Presto 07062 earns credit for storage, and the bella models for removable probes and dishwasher-safe parts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at wattage and temperature ranges where listed. The bella XL states 1500 watts and the Gourmia gives 200 to 400F, while others offer less detail.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grease and safety design
howWeEvaluated.description: Drip trays, ledges, cool-touch bodies and handles were compared. The Gourmia leads on grease, the Presto 07030 on a cool-touch low profile and the bella XL on a built-in ledge.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at the upper cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Lineup positioning is clear: bella 12 by 22 for balance, the warming-tray bella for batches, Gourmia for grease, Presto 07062 for storage, Presto 07030 for buffets and bella XL for power. Scores reflect product specs and buyer feedback, not hands-on trials.

howToChoose.intro: How the heat is set changes how you wash and store.

cards.label: Removable probe
cards.text: The bella 12 by 22 inch models use a removable temperature probe, which lets the plate be washed without the control. The probe has to be seated before cooking and kept dry. Choose probe control if you value precision and washing ease.

cards.label: Built-in controls
cards.text: Models such as the Gourmia and Presto list ranges or controls without describing a removable probe. They remove one setup step but may limit how thoroughly you can wash the body. Choose built-in if you prefer fewer parts.

howToChoose.note: Probe for washing, built-in for simplicity. Whichever you pick, store the probe where it will not get knocked or splashed, because a lost or damaged probe leaves the plate unusable.

faq.q: Is a 22 inch griddle too big for a home kitchen?
faq.a: It can be. A 22 inch plate needs generous counter space while it heats and a wide shelf for storage. Models with detachable handles, like the Presto 07062, help. If you cook for one or two, a smaller plate is a better fit. Many owners find that the biggest plate gets used mainly on weekends, so weigh how often you will really feed a crowd before committing the shelf space.

faq.q: Does the warming tray model cook differently?
faq.a: The main plate is the same 12 by 22 inch size as the standard bella. The warming tray is a separate piece that keeps cooked food ready to serve. It adds convenience but also bulk. The tray earns its keep when you cook several rounds, and it is wasted if every meal comes off the plate in a single pass.

The Gourmia has a pull-out drip tray built for the job. The Presto and bella listings describe no drain, so blot fat with paper towels. For regular bacon, drainage should decide your choice. Cooking bacon in a single layer and removing finished strips promptly also stops grease from pooling around the edges of any flat plate.

No. Ceramic needs nylon or wooden tools, and metal can scratch the surface. A thin film of oil before cooking helps food release. Silicone turners work well too, and plastic spatulas with rounded edges are a safe alternative if you do not own nylon ones.

faq.q: How should I wash a large plate?
faq.a: Let it cool fully first. The bella models list dishwasher-safe parts, and the probe must stay dry. A plate this size rarely fits a sink, so wipe it down while it is still warm and then rinse. Never submerge the heating base or the probe socket, and let the plate dry fully before storing so moisture does not linger under the coating.

It helps with heat recovery on a large plate. The bella XL lists it, but even coverage matters as much as the number. Preheat fully before cooking. On a plate this long, rotating food from the cooler end to the hotter end also evens out browning when your counter outlet or cord placement leaves one side slightly warmer.

faq.q: Are cool-touch handles the same as a cool body?
faq.a: No. The bella XL has cool-touch handles for moving it, while the Presto 07030 has a cool-touch body. The cooking surface on both stays hot, so keep children away. Set the griddle on a heat-safe, level surface with space behind it, and leave the cord out of walkways so nobody catches it.
